summary: NHTSA revised the final EIS in response to comments, including dropping the sulfate emissions discussion entirely and revising the noble metal use section to reflect a smaller increase in platinum and palladium use; gasoline savings were also restructured to cover a range of fuel economy levels and two NPA classes.
text:
As a result of the analysis of all comments the agency is making several changes to the draft EIS. Gasoline savings are described in this final EIS relative to a range of fuel economies. The range was established by applying the maximum and minimum possible fuel economy penalties of the MY 1979 emission standard to the originally proposed AFES. Also, gasoline savings are shown for two classes of NPA's. The two classes are 1) recreational type NPA's with off-road capability and 2) all other NPA's.

The effects of the MY 1979 emission standard for California, according to the information applied by the domestic manufacturers, are incorporated. The manufacturers' comments on the impossibility of weight reduction are not incorporated because the application of weight reduction is only to GM and they did not say it was impossible. The discussion of sulfate emissions has been dropped and the discussion of noble metal use has been revised to indicate a smaller increase in the use of platinum and palladium.

closing_anchor: The discussion of sulfate emissions has been dropped and the discussion of noble metal use has been revised to indicate a smaller increase in the use of platinum and palladium.
